own_solution.law: Photon energy is hc/lambda = 3.1 eV. With emission probability eta and complete collection, I = e eta P/(hc/lambda) = 0.003(0.005)/3.1 A.
assumptions: The stated emission probability applies to all incident photons of the specified wavelength.
The stated optical power reaches the cathode, and all released electrons are collected.
The question concerns the current during the present measurement.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: T306C and TE41A replace the explicit 3.4 mW used in their corresponding extra-power variants with unspecified amounts, violating the requirement that variants preserve the same number and unit.

counterexamples: T306C permits an additional chart illumination of 1 mW, whereas TEB4A specifies 3.4 mW, so these renderings do not preserve the quantity.
TE41A permits an earlier additional cathode illumination of 1 mW, whereas TC8F7 specifies 3.4 mW.
notes: The base physics and each individual current calculation are well-posed. The invalid verdict concerns the required numerical matching between sentence variants.
